From d769711fcddd005f1e654b3bde547140917fe696 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nicolin Chen <nicolinc@nvidia.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2026 18:15:20 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] iommu: Fix NULL group->domain dereference in
 pci_dev_reset_iommu_done()

Local sashiko review pointed it out that group->domain could be NULL when
a default domain fails to allocate during the first probe, which can crash
at domain->ops->attach_dev dereference in __iommu_attach_device() invoked
by pci_dev_reset_iommu_done().

pci_dev_reset_iommu_prepare() is fine as an old_domain pointer can be NULL.

Skip the re-attach in pci_dev_reset_iommu_done() to fix the bug.

Fixes: c279e83953d9 ("iommu: Introduce pci_dev_reset_iommu_prepare/done()")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Nicolin Chen <nicolinc@nvidia.com>
Reviewed-by: Lu Baolu <baolu.lu@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Joerg Roedel <joerg.roedel@amd.com>

diff --git a/drivers/iommu/iommu.c b/drivers/iommu/iommu.c
index 61c12ba78206..b8847cc43e76 100644
--- a/drivers/iommu/iommu.c
+++ b/drivers/iommu/iommu.c
@@ -4073,8 +4073,13 @@ void pci_dev_reset_iommu_done(struct pci_dev *pdev)
 	if (WARN_ON(!group->blocking_domain))
 		return;
 
-	/* Re-attach RID domain back to group->domain */
-	if (group->domain != group->blocking_domain) {
+	/*
+	 * Re-attach RID domain back to group->domain
+	 *
+	 * Leave the device parked in the blocking_domain if group->domain isn't
+	 * initialized yet
+	 */
+	if (group->domain && group->domain != group->blocking_domain) {
 		WARN_ON(__iommu_attach_device(group->domain, &pdev->dev,
 					      group->blocking_domain));
 	}
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies the `pci_dev_reset_iommu_done()` function in `drivers/iommu/iommu.c` to prevent a NULL pointer dereference when `group->domain` is not initialized.

**Modifications in each file:**
- **drivers/iommu/iommu.c**: Added a check for `group->domain` being non-NULL before comparing it with `group->blocking_domain` and before calling `__iommu_attach_device()`. Also added a comment explaining that if `group->domain` is NULL (e.g., due to a failed default domain allocation), the device should remain parked in the blocking domain.

**Relationships:**
- The bug occurred because `pci_dev_reset_iommu_done()` assumed `group->domain` was always valid, leading to a crash when calling `domain->ops->attach_dev`. The fix adds a guard condition (`if (group->domain && ...)`) to skip the re-attachment when `group->domain` is NULL, thus avoiding the dereference. This is consistent with `pci_dev_reset_iommu_prepare()`, which already tolerates a NULL `old_domain` pointer. The change ensures safe behavior when the default domain failed to allocate during the first probe.

Here is the commit message:
iommu: Fix NULL group->domain dereference in
 pci_dev_reset_iommu_done()

Local sashiko review pointed it out that group->domain could be NULL when
a default domain fails to allocate during the first probe, which can crash
at domain->ops->attach_dev dereference in __iommu_attach_device() invoked
by pci_dev_reset_iommu_done().

pci_dev_reset_iommu_prepare() is fine as an old_domain pointer can be NULL.

Skip the re-attach in pci_dev_reset_iommu_done() to fix the bug.

Fixes: c279e83953d9 ("iommu: Introduce pci_dev_reset_iommu_prepare/done()")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Nicolin Chen <nicolinc@nvidia.com>
Reviewed-by: Lu Baolu <baolu.lu@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Joerg Roedel <joerg.roedel@amd.com>

Here is the root cause:
The function `pci_dev_reset_iommu_done()` in `iommu.c` dereferences `group->domain` without a NULL check, causing a crash when `group->domain` is NULL because a default domain failed to allocate during the first device probe.

Here is the patch:
  */
 void pci_dev_reset_iommu_done(struct pci_dev *pdev)
 {
 	struct iommu_group *group = pdev->dev.iommu_group;
 	unsigned long pasid;
 	void *entry;
 
 	if (!pci_ats_supported(pdev) || !dev_has_iommu(&pdev->dev))
 		return;
 
 	guard(mutex)(&group->mutex);
 
 	/* pci_dev_reset_iommu_prepare() was bypassed for the device */
 	if (!group->resetting_domain)
 		return;
 
 	/* pci_dev_reset_iommu_prepare() was not successfully called */
 	if (WARN_ON(!group->blocking_domain))
 		return;
 
-	/* Re-attach RID domain back to group->domain */
-	if (group->domain != group->blocking_domain) {
+	/*
+	 * Re-attach RID domain back to group->domain
+	 *
+	 * Leave the device parked in the blocking_domain if group->domain isn't
+	 * initialized yet
+	 */
+	if (group->domain && group->domain != group->blocking_domain) {
 		WARN_ON(__iommu_attach_device(group->domain, &pdev->dev,
 					      group->blocking_domain));
 	}
 
 	/*
 	 * Re-attach PASID domains back to the domains retained in pasid_array.
 	 *
 	 * The pasid_array is mostly fenced by group->mutex, except one reader
 	 * in iommu_attach_handle_get(), so it's safe to read without xa_lock.
 	 */
 	xa_for_each_start(&group->pasid_array, pasid, entry, 1)
 		WARN_ON(__iommu_set_group_pasid(
 			pasid_array_entry_to_domain(entry), group, pasid,
 			group->blocking_domain));
 
 	group->resetting_domain = NULL;
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(pci_dev_reset_iommu_done);

    WARN_ON(__iommu_attach_device(group->domain, &pdev->dev, group->blocking_domain));
}
Reason:
The added NULL check (`group->domain`) ensures the re-attach is only attempted when `group->domain` is valid, preventing the NULL pointer dereference. If `group->domain` is NULL, the device remains safely parked in the blocking domain.
